title: Eurostat euro-area HICP, complete August 2026 data — the component detail behind the 3.3% flash
source: EST: ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/products-euro-indicators/w/2-01092026-ap — the August 2026 flash-estimate release, fetched direct 2026-09-08 by the cpi-2026-09-11 D-3 pulse-check adjacency sweep. The page names the follow-up outright: 'Complete data for August is scheduled for release on September 17, 2026.' The same release carries the flash itself, quoted verbatim: 'Euro area annual inflation is expected to be 3.3% in August 2026, up from 2.9% in July', with components energy 14.3% y/y (from 10.3%), services 3.0% (from 3.3%), non-energy industrial goods 1.2% (from 0.9%) and food, alcohol & tobacco 1.2% (stable). Corroborated by the sibling flash release for July, 2-19082026-ap ('Annual inflation up to 2.9% in the euro area'), which puts the same flash-then-complete cadence on the record. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, and because this calendar carries no confirmed source prefix for a non-US statistical agency — the same taxonomy reason ecb-decision-2026-09-10 is filed estimate despite a direct ECB primary. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the cpi-2026-09-11 D-3 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08), and it earns a row for a coverage gap rather than for a price channel. This calendar tracks EIGHT ECB entries (decision, account, quiet periods, bank lending survey, monetary developments) and ZERO Eurostat inflation releases — which is why the euro area's August HICP flash, published 2026-09-01, did not reach the US CPI ledger until a week later, despite being the first hard August-window inflation reading from a comparable advanced economy inside the identical energy shock. Its shape is why it matters: the acceleration to 3.3% is almost entirely ENERGY (14.3% y/y) while SERVICES DECELERATED (3.3% -> 3.0%), which corroborates the energy-hot / core-tame shape the cpi-2026-09-11 ledger has assumed since D-25. The 09-17 complete release is where that split is confirmed or revised against the flash, with the full component detail the flash omits. Impact LOW and symbols empty, deliberately: no house playbook is rates-keyed, no tracked name carries euro-rates or euro-inflation exposure, and a complete release two weeks after a flash almost never moves a tape — what the entry buys is that the NEXT US inflation sweep sees the euro-area read on its own calendar instead of missing it for a week. Sequencing note for whoever researches it: 09-17 sits AFTER both ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and fomc-2026-09-16, so it is the first euro-area inflation detail published into a post-FOMC rate backdrop, and it is the release against which the ECB's 09-10 decision (~88% priced for +25bp to a 2.50% deposit rate) can be judged. Read-across limit, stated so it is not overread later: euro HICP is NOT US core CPI — it carries no owners'-equivalent-rent, where US core's heaviest weight sits, and its energy weight is higher, so any comparison is directional and never quantitative. Proposed as an estimate; it widens caution and licenses nothing.
